title: profiling-smoke-regression-pipeline-and-collectors
body:
SUMMARY:
This is a working note for a lightweight, repeatable profiling smoke/regression pipeline and the small collector/utility scripts we use to capture traces on CI and dev boxes. Goal: give devs and SREs a simple entrypoint to detect regressions in per-request p99 latency and allocation hot paths without running a full perf lab run.

WHY THIS EXISTS:
- Current perf CI jobs are heavy and take hours; we need a fast gateway check that runs in ~10–20 minutes.
- The smoke pipeline should exercise the common request patterns (chat single-turn, streaming token loops, and embeddings) and validate no new alloc/CPU hotspots were introduced.
- Outputs: condensed flamegraph (SVG), a small summary CSV with p50/p90/p99 for CPU and wall-time, and a compressed trace (.tar.gz) for deeper analysis.

PRINCIPLES:
- Non-invasive: prefer sampling (perf/eBPF) over heavy instrumentation.
- Deterministic-ish: use synthetic workloads with a fixed seed and short KV-cache warmup.
- Quick feedback: pipeline must fit within CI job timeouts (<= 30m).
- Reproducible: record exact binary+model+env (docker image sha, kernel version).

QUICK START (local dev):
Assumes: Linux dev box, Rust/C++ runtime binary at ./bin/runtime, docker available for pulling test model image.
1) Warmup + baseline run (single-thread):
   ./scripts/warmup_kv_cache.sh --model t5-small --rpc localhost:8080 --requests 50
   time ./scripts/smoke_client.py --concurrency 1 --requests 200 --mode chat --seed 42 > smoke_raw.log 2>&1

2) Run lightweight sampler (eBPF) for CPU stacks during the same workload (requires sudo):
   sudo ./scripts/ebpf_sampler.sh --pid $(pgrep -f "bin/runtime") --duration 600 --out /tmp/smoke-sample.data

3) Convert sample -> folded stacks -> flamegraph.svg
   ./tools/stackcollapse-ebpf.py /tmp/smoke-sample.data > /tmp/stacks.folded
   ./tools/flamegraph.pl /tmp/stacks.folded > artifacts/flamegraph-smoke.svg

4) Run allocation sampler (optional):
   sudo ./scripts/heaptrack-wrapper.sh --pid $(pgrep -f "bin/runtime") --out artifacts/heap-smoke.gz --duration 600

CI JOB FLOW (high level):
- Trigger: PR to serving-runtime or daily-batch (canary branch).
- Stage A: spin up a minimal runtime in a docker task with deterministic env (use test model and pinned weights).
- Stage B: run smoke_client.py workload and capture request timings into metrics exporter (pushgateway).
- Stage C (parallel): run ebpf_sampler and a — short — perf record for native symbols.
- Stage D: post-process artifacts producing: flamegraph.svg, perf.data.gz, smoke-summary.csv.
- Stage E: upload artifacts to GCS at gs://r-inference/cicd/profiling/<date>/<sha>/ and attach URLs to CI comment.
- Failure criteria: p99 wall-time increased > 15% vs baseline OR new top-N cumulative CPU frames not seen in baseline.

NOTES ON SAMPLERS:
- eBPF sampler: our light wrapper collects stack traces at a 200Hz rate using a small BPF program (scripts/ebpf_sampler.c -> compiled at CI). Keep this low to avoid perturbation.
- perf record fallback: perf works when running on machines with perf_event enabled; record for 30s samples at 100Hz to keep perf.data size small.
- heaptrack / jemalloc profiling: enabled only for nightly runs; heaptrack adds overhead and should be gated by an env flag.

ARTIFACTS AND NAMING CONVENTION:
- artifacts/<job>/<sha>/flamegraph-smoke.svg
- artifacts/<job>/<sha>/smoke-summary.csv  (columns: route, mode, concurrency, p50_ms, p90_ms, p99_ms, cpu_p99_ms, allocations_delta)
- artifacts/<job>/<sha>/perf.data.gz

SMOKE CLIENT BEHAVIOR (implementation notes):
- Runs 3 scenarios back-to-back: chat-single-turn (prompt len 64), streaming-token-loop (generate 128 tokens with stream), embeddings-batch (batch size 8).
- Each scenario has a deterministic random seed and a small KV-cache warmup of 20 requests before measuring.
- Reports timings to stdout and to a local JSON summary for the post-processor.

POST-PROCESSING STEPS (ci job script):
1) Verify smoke-summary.json exists and parse p99s. If p99 growth > threshold, mark job FAILED.
2) If sampler artifacts present, run stackcollapse and flamegraph.pl to produce an SVG.
3) Compute "delta-frames": top-10 frames by cumulative CPU time vs baseline. Upload both lists for triage.

COMMON TROUBLESHOOTING / GOTCHAS:
- Empty flamegraph: usually symbolication failed. Ensure the binary is built with frame pointers or DWARF (we prefer frame pointers for production builds).
- No samples for runtime threads: eBPF sampler may filter threads; check sampler PID and thread collection flags.
- Noise: reduce sample frequency or increase run duration if flamegraph is sparse. But keep CI duration budget in mind.
- Kernel perf disabled in CI images – add CAP_SYS_ADMIN or choose a host runner with perf enabled.

SMALL SCRIPTS & TOOLS (location):
- scripts/ebpf_sampler.sh  -> wrapper to compile and run the BPF program, rotates output, respects CI_MAX_TIME env var.
- tools/stackcollapse-ebpf.py -> converts raw bpf format into folded stacks.
- scripts/warmup_kv_cache.sh -> sends N short requests to populate server KV caches.
- tools/flamegraph.pl -> stock script (checked-in copy pinned to v0.6).

EXAMPLE CI JOB YAML (sketch):
- job: runtime-smoke-profiling
  runs-on: self-hosted-perf
  steps:
    - checkout
    - setup-docker
    - run: docker run --rm -d --name smoke-runtime my-registry/runtime:ci-<sha>
    - run: ./scripts/ci_run_smoke.sh --out-dir artifacts/$GITHUB_SHA
    - run: ./scripts/ci_postprocess.sh artifacts/$GITHUB_SHA || (cat artifacts/$GITHUB_SHA/smoke-summary.csv && exit 1)
    - upload-artifact: artifacts/$GITHUB_SHA

WHEN TO USE THIS VS FULL PERF LAB:
Use this pipeline for fast regression detection on PRs or daily canaries. If smoke pipeline flags a regression, schedule a full perf lab run (longer duration, larger load, full heap and cpu traces, hardware counters).

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs:
- Threshold tuning: current p99 delta 15% is a placeholder. Need to establish per-route baselines and seasonally adjust.
- Golden baseline storage: where to keep long-term baselines for delta comparisons (queryable DB?).
- Symbolication at scale: consider uploading binaries to a symbol server for CI to fetch and symbolicate automatically.
- eBPF program maintenance: consolidate with ebpf-light-sampler repo vs keep a trimmed copy in this repo.

LINKS / REFERENCES:
- GH PR with early prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/317
- Related tickets: RINF-842 (smoke profiling pipeline), RINF-921 (ci artifact storage)

NOTES TO SELF:
- Demo this in the "serving-runtime" weekly sync next Tuesday; bring SVGs and smoke-summary.csv for the last 3 commits.
- If showing to PMs, prepare a 2-slide summary: what we measure, why it matters, cost to run vs benefit.

END OF NOTE
